audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s broad Ancient Near Eastern Studies route examines ancient Egypt, the Near East, Greece and Rome through history, religion, archaeology, material culture and written sources. It provides orientation in languages and writing systems alongside museum and heritage study. Specialist ancient-language training belongs to the other tracks.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The table retains 155 EC of distinct listed content, counting repeated courses and the two versions of the same Philosophy of Science core course once. The remaining 25 EC, its year allocation and entry to the Roman North Africa seminar still need confirmation. The full curriculum and UCR comparison remain unfinished.

curriculum.limitation: Distinct listed content: 155 of 180 EC. The remaining 25 EC and Philosophy of Science year allocation are unresolved. Roman North Africa entry and related Ancient History seminar progression still need confirmation; full first- and second-year completion for the thesis also depends on the curriculum repair.

componentNotes.ono03: First-year students take this seminar alongside History of the Ancient Near East. Its repeated listing does not add a second 5 EC to this partial inventory.
componentNotes.ono04: Counted once for 5 EC. The curriculum lists two versions of the same core course; its correct year allocation remains under review.
componentNotes.ono05: Successful completion is part of the first-year study-advice requirements, together with Written Sources of the Ancient Near East and the language panorama. This is a 10 EC seminar, not extra credit for each repeated reference.
componentNotes.ono06: Successful completion forms part of the route’s first-year study-advice requirements.
componentNotes.ono08: Successful completion forms part of the route’s first-year study-advice requirements.
componentNotes.ono18: Entry requires successful completion of Ancient History and meeting the study-advice threshold.
componentNotes.ono19: One of two approved 10 EC second-year choices. Entry for this route requires Ancient History and the first-year Ancient Near Eastern Studies seminar. Confirmation is still needed that the current seminar meets the applicable thematic-seminar requirement for this cohort.
componentNotes.ono20: The 5 EC thesis seminar requires completion of the first two bachelor years. An exception requires consultation with the study adviser and examination-board permission. Its work supports the separate 10 EC thesis.
componentNotes.ono21: Entry is stated for students who completed the History first year and both second-year History seminars, including one in the same field. Greek and Latin Language and Culture students are also eligible. Ordinary entry from this Ancient Near Eastern Studies route remains unconfirmed.
componentNotes.ono22: The 10 EC thesis requires completion of the first two bachelor years and participation in the thesis seminar. The topic and research approach are agreed with the supervisor, whose appointment requires examination-board approval. The thesis has a maximum of 10,000 words, including footnotes and excluding the bibliography and appendices. Full year-one and year-two completion remains dependent on the curriculum repair.
componentNotes.ono23: 30 EC in the first semester of year three for a minor, approved courses, an approved internship or study abroad. An individual course package needs approval and normally permits at most 10 EC at level 100 and requires at least 10 EC at level 300 or above. Courses must avoid overlap with compulsory study; Honours College courses cannot count. Recognized full 30 EC minors at Leiden, Delft or Erasmus generally need no separate approval. An internship requires prior approval; a placement or study-abroad place is not guaranteed.
